chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the place of the forehead of the one prostrating, can it be higher than the place of standing? He said: No, but it should be even.
And in another hadith regarding prostration on raised ground, he said: If the place of your forehead is higher than your legs by the measure of a brick, there is no problem.
ai.seo_question: What is the permissible height difference for the forehead during prostration in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of sujood by distinguishing between the general principle that the forehead should be level with the feet and the practical concession for uneven ground. It establishes that a minor elevation, up to the height of a brick (approximately 3-4 cm), does not invalidate the prayer, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (yusr) in ritual purity and prostration.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the place for the forehead of the one performing Sajdah. Can it happen to be higher than the (place of) standing?’ Heasws said: ‘No, but it should happen to be even’.

And in another Hadeeth regarding the Sujūd (plural of Sajdah) upon the raised ground, heasws said: ‘If it was so that the place of your forehead was higher than (the place of) your legs of the measurement of a brick, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the place of Sujud (prostration) if it can be higher than the place where one stands. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it must be level.’
In another Hadith about the place of Sujud (prostration) which is higher than the place on which one stands, it is said that if it is of the height of a brick it is not harmful.’”
